claim: Anthropic open-sourced MCP on Nov 25, 2024 as 'a universal, open standard for connecting AI systems with data sources'; initial SDKs and reference servers for Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres, Puppeteer.
quote: Today, we're open-sourcing the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a new standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data lives.

claim: MCP history: announced Nov 25, 2024 by Anthropic; created by David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers; OpenAI adopted Mar 2025; Google DeepMind followed.
quote: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard and open-source framework introduced by Anthropic in November 2024.

claim: Anthropic donated MCP to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation on Dec 9, 2025; AAIF co-founded by Anthropic, Block, OpenAI with Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare, Bloomberg.
quote: The Model Context Protocol's governance model will remain unchanged: the project's maintainers will continue to prioritize community input and transparent decision-making.

claim: MCP Dev Summit NYC April 2-3 2026 drew ~1,200 attendees; David Soria Parra reported 110M+ monthly SDK downloads; Uber/Nordstrom/Bloomberg/Duolingo/PwC keynotes showed production deployments.
quote: MCP had more than 110 million SDK downloads every single month.

claim: Current MCP spec version is 2025-11-25; defines JSON-RPC 2.0 message format, stateful connections, capability negotiation between Hosts, Clients, and Servers.
quote: The protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0 messages to establish communication between: Hosts: LLM applications that initiate connections; Clients: Connectors within the host application; Servers: Services that provide context and capabilities.

claim: 2026-07-28 release candidate introduces stateless protocol core, Extensions framework, Tasks extension, MCP Apps, authorization hardening, 12-month formal deprecation policy, JSON Schema 2020-12 support.
quote: A remote MCP server that previously needed sticky sessions, a shared session store, and deep packet inspection at the gateway can now run behind a plain round-robin load balancer.

claim: The MCP specification repository is the canonical home of the protocol schema and SEP process.
quote: Specification and documentation for the Model Context Protocol

claim: Client features: Sampling lets a server request LLM completions through the client; Roots scope filesystem access (file:// URIs); Elicitation lets a server request structured input from the user mid-tool-call.
quote: Server-side features like Tools, Resources, and Prompts let you expose powerful capabilities in a structured, reusable way, while client-side features including Sampling, Roots, and Elicitation ensure that these capabilities are used efficiently, safely, and with the user always in control.

claim: Sampling is deprecated as of draft 2026-v1 and will be supported for at least 1 year after that release.
quote: The Sampling feature is deprecated as of protocol version DRAFT-2026-v1 and will continue to be supported in any version of MCP released within 1 year of DRAFT-2026-v1.

claim: Two standard transports: stdio (local subprocess, JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout) and Streamable HTTP (single endpoint, POST+GET with optional SSE for streaming); the older HTTP+SSE transport was deprecated in the 2025-03-26 spec.
quote: Streamable HTTP is JSON-RPC 2.0 over one HTTP endpoint that supports POST and GET, with optional Server-Sent Events for streaming.

claim: MCP servers act as OAuth 2.1 Resource Servers; clients MUST implement RFC 8707 Resource Indicators and discover auth servers via RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata; PKCE with SHA-256 is mandatory; stdio transports skip OAuth and use env-based credentials.
quote: MCP clients MUST implement Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0 as defined in RFC 8707 to explicitly specify the target resource for which the token is being requested.

claim: One year after launch MCP had 16,000+ servers; Sam Altman: 'people love MCP and we are excited to add support across our products'; Demis Hassabis: 'MCP is a good protocol and it's rapidly becoming an open standard'.
quote: people love MCP and we are excited to add support across our products

claim: Community-maintained 'awesome' index of MCP servers; one of the primary discovery surfaces for the ecosystem.
quote: A collection of MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers.

claim: Official MCP reference-servers monorepo: filesystem, fetch, git, sequential-thinking, memory, time, and more.
quote: Model Context Protocol Servers

claim: Microsoft's Playwright MCP server gives agents a deterministic, accessibility-tree-driven browser — currently the most popular browser-automation MCP.
quote: Playwright Model Context Protocol server

claim: GitHub's official MCP server exposes repos, PRs, issues, and search — the canonical example of vendor-built MCP.
quote: GitHub's official MCP Server

claim: Context7 streams up-to-date library docs into the model context window via MCP — a 'just-in-time' alternative to RAG for codegen.
quote: Context7 MCP Server - Up-to-date code documentation for LLMs

claim: FastMCP is the Pythonic high-level framework for MCP servers; v3.0 (Jan 19, 2026) added component versioning, granular authorization, and OpenTelemetry; now maintained under PrefectHQ.
quote: The fast, Pythonic way to build MCP servers and clients.

claim: Official quickstart for building an MCP server with the Python SDK / FastMCP, plus stdio launch and Claude Desktop wiring.
quote: Build an MCP server

claim: MCP facilitates integrations between LLMs and 3rd-party data sources; A2A (Google, April 2025) supports interoperability between AI agents — they are complementary layers, not competitors.
quote: MCP facilitates integrations between LLMs and 3rd-party data sources, while A2A supports interoperability between AI agents.

claim: Function calling is per-vendor JSON schema; MCP is a vendor-neutral transport that lets one tool integration work across all models; A2A is for agent-to-agent task delegation.
quote: Function Calling, popularized by OpenAI and now adopted by Meta, Google, and others, was the first mainstream approach to connecting LLMs with external tools.

claim: Simon Willison's 'lethal trifecta': private data + exposure to untrusted instructions + exfiltration vector = guaranteed prompt-injection exposure when any MCP host mixes them.
quote: any time you mix together tools that can perform actions on the user's behalf with exposure to potentially untrusted input you're effectively allowing attackers to make those tools do whatever they want

claim: Curated timeline of 13+ MCP security incidents Apr 2025–Apr 2026: WhatsApp tool poisoning, GitHub MCP injection, mcp-remote RCE (CVE-2025-6514), Smithery breach, Postmark supply-chain, Figma command injection, nginx-ui RCE, and more.
quote: silently exfiltrate a user's entire WhatsApp history

claim: Public scans in 2026 identified up to ~200,000 vulnerable MCP instances exposed across IDEs, internal tools, and cloud services.
quote: A 2026 disclosure exposed up to 200,000 vulnerable MCP instances across IDEs, internal tools, and cloud services.

claim: The 2026 MCP roadmap reorganises around priority areas (transport, agent communication, governance, enterprise readiness) rather than dates; Tasks moved to extension; Working Groups own delivery.
quote: The new document is organized around priority areas, rather than around dates.

claim: MCP Apps (SEP-1865) shipped Jan 26, 2026 as the first official MCP extension: servers ship interactive HTML rendered in a sandboxed iframe; UI talks back over JSON-RPC, so every action still hits the host's consent and audit paths.
quote: MCP Apps - Bringing UI Capabilities To MCP Clients

claim: Reference SDK and spec for the MCP Apps extension; ui:// URI scheme; iframe sandboxing; bi-directional postMessage bridged to JSON-RPC.
quote: Official repo for spec & SDK of MCP Apps protocol - standard for UIs embedded AI chatbots, served by MCP servers

claim: Tasks extension reshapes the lifecycle around the stateless core: server returns a task handle; client polls tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel — designed for long-running enterprise workflows.
quote: A tool call may be appropriate for a quick lookup or short operation, but enterprise workflows often involve background work, retries, waiting for external systems, human review, or coordination across multiple services.

claim: MCP Inspector is the official browser-based debugger for MCP servers (connect, list capabilities, exercise tools/resources/prompts) — the standard live-demo surface.
quote: Visual testing tool for MCP servers

claim: Official MCP Registry, backed by Anthropic, GitHub, PulseMCP and Microsoft — the upstream metadata source for discoverability and supply-chain provenance.
quote: Community-driven registry service for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers
